claim: Of the campaign's 10,319 openings with a lintel, 60% continue the facade's own tile above the mouth, yet 74% of its 8,320 rooms with more than one wall tile put a different tile on their two-sided walls (jambs, reveals) than on their solid ones: the opening tile is a property of the material, the dressing goes on the reveals of openings, and the band above a mouth belongs to the facade. 45% of two-sided walkable walls are seams between sectors of one space, not apertures at all.
evidence: knowledge/blood/design/apertures-v1.json (43 maps): lintel.openings_with_one 10,319, continues_the_facade 0.599; kinds.seam 25,594 of 56,624 (0.452); lintel_owner: the upper section takes the wall's own picnum. The earlier '70% of 10,475 lintels' is not in the file as it stands (re-read 2026-11-26)
Painting a whole portal wall in the opening tile hung a 4.35-body sheet of ashlar over a doorway in a rubble wall, because Build draws the upper section from the wall's own picnum.
8,320 campaign rooms, 74% of them: a role-separated census over the campaign (projects/blood-city/level/materials.py:23)
use: Give every material an opening tile and apply it to the reveals of its portal walls, not to the band above a mouth; when an opening looks wrong, find who owns the band above it before touching tiles; exclude seams when measuring apertures.
